findings: The answer directly states the 1-or-2 result under explicit ordinary-int/two-completed-thread assumptions instead of hiding prerequisites.
It distinguishes atomic single int access from non-atomic compound i++ and gives both lost-update and serialized interleavings.
The Java memory-model explanation correctly separates worker-worker data race from join-based main-thread completion visibility.
The exact candidate bytecode independently shows load/add/store decomposition; deterministic fixtures witness the two result interleavings without relying on probabilistic scheduler reproduction.
Repeated synchronized and AtomicInteger checks validate both safe alternatives.
The answer avoids the common overclaim that data races permit literally arbitrary int results or that volatile makes compound increment atomic.
